item.content:encoded:
The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offering a valuable opportunity for selected nonprofit organizations to transform their existing software and technology projects into publicly accessible, licensed and well-documented open source tools — at no cost to participating organizations. The partnership brings together Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward to support a small group of technology-focused nonprofits with the technical expertise, student developer capacity and industry mentorship needed to prepare software for open source use or strengthen projects that are already part of the open source ecosystem. As part of the program, each selected nonprofit will receive a dedicated team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers who will work on the organization’s project for 16 weeks. The program represents approximately 800 hours of technical work per team, supported by weekly check-ins, technical guidance, project management assistance and team coaching. The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have developed useful technology but lack the time, staff capacity or specialised expertise required to properly license, document, package and maintain that technology as an open source resource.

Applications for the program close on September 9, 2026.

Nonprofit Open Source Partnership 2026 at a Glance

  • Program: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership
  • Organizing partners: Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward
  • Target applicants: Selected technology-focused nonprofit organizations
  • Project focus: Open sourcing an existing nonprofit software tool or contributing to an existing open source project
  • Technical support: Eight college student volunteer developers per nonprofit
  • Program duration: 16 weeks
  • Technical contribution: Approximately 800 hours per team
  • Industry mentorship: Bloomberg employee volunteers
  • Open source guidance: CodeDay
  • Program support: Develop for Good
  • Cost: No cost to participating nonprofits
  • Nonprofit application deadline: September 9, 2026
  • Selection notification: October 2, 2026
  • Program kickoff: October 25, 2026
  • Final delivery: February 20, 2027

What Is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership?

Many nonprofit organizations build or use technology to deliver their missions, but creating software and preparing it for open source distribution are two different challenges.

A nonprofit may have an existing application, platform, internal tool or other technology that could potentially benefit other organizations. However, making that technology genuinely open source involves much more than publishing code online.

The organization may need to address:

  • Software licensing
  • Technical documentation
  • Code organization
  • Developer onboarding
  • Project contribution processes
  • Technical maintenance
  • User documentation
  • Open source best practices
  • Project management
  • Quality assurance
  • Collaboration with external developers

These tasks require time and specialised technical knowledge that many nonprofits may not have available internally.

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is designed to help close this gap.

Through the partnership, participating organizations receive a dedicated team of student developers and support from experienced professionals who can help turn an existing technology project into a more accessible and reusable open source resource.

Who Is Behind the Program?

The initiative is a collaboration between four organizations:

Bloomberg

Bloomberg is participating in the partnership through employee volunteers who will provide guidance and mentorship to participating nonprofit projects.

Develop for Good

Develop for Good provides the student development teams and program support. The organization will run weekly check-ins with participating students and provide structured support covering technical work, project management and team coaching.

CodeDay

CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices, helping participating nonprofits understand how to prepare their projects for open source use.

Fast Forward

Fast Forward is also part of the partnership, contributing to an initiative designed to strengthen technology capacity within the nonprofit sector.

Together, these organizations provide a combination of student technical talent, professional mentorship, open source expertise and program management support.

What Will Selected Nonprofits Receive?

Selected organizations will receive several forms of support throughout the 16-week program.

1. A Dedicated Team of Eight Student Developers

Each participating nonprofit will receive a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers.

The students will dedicate their time to the nonprofit’s selected project throughout the 16-week program.

This gives nonprofits access to a substantial pool of technical capacity without the financial cost associated with hiring a conventional software development team.

2. Approximately 800 Hours of Technical Work

The program estimates that each team will contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work.

This can provide significant development capacity for a nonprofit that may otherwise struggle to dedicate internal resources to an open source initiative.

The exact nature of the work will depend on the organization’s project and the objectives established for the program.

Potential work could involve preparing an existing tool for open source publication, improving documentation or contributing to an existing open source project.

3. Weekly Program Check-Ins

Develop for Good will conduct weekly check-ins with students throughout the program.

These check-ins are designed to help teams remain focused, address challenges and maintain progress toward the project’s objectives.

4. Technical Support

Participating teams will receive structured technical support to help them move their projects forward.

This can be especially valuable for organizations that have a strong mission and a useful technology product but do not have extensive internal software engineering capacity.

5. Project Management Support

The partnership also includes project management assistance.

This helps keep the work organized and ensures that the student development team and nonprofit point-of-contact remain aligned on priorities, deliverables and timelines.

6. Team Coaching

Teams will receive coaching designed to support effective collaboration and project execution.

Because the program involves nonprofit staff, student developers and industry mentors, structured coaching can help ensure that different participants remain coordinated throughout the 16-week engagement.

7. Open Source Best-Practices Guidance

CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices.

This is particularly important for nonprofits that are making the transition from an internally developed or privately maintained tool to a publicly accessible project.

8. Bloomberg Employee Mentorship

Participating nonprofits will receive weekly guidance from experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers.

These mentors are described as being invested in the success of the projects and can provide an additional professional perspective throughout the program.

9. A Publicly Accessible and Documented Final Product

One of the most important outcomes is a finished project that is intended to be:

  • Publicly accessible
  • Properly licensed
  • Documented
  • Ready for the nonprofit to use
  • Potentially useful to other organizations

This can extend the impact of a nonprofit’s technology beyond its immediate internal use.

What Does “Open Source” Mean for Participating Nonprofits?

Open source software is software whose source code is made available under a license that allows others to access, use and, depending on the license, modify and redistribute it under defined conditions.

For a nonprofit, making a tool open source can create opportunities for other organizations, developers and communities to benefit from technology that might otherwise remain limited to the organization that originally developed it.

However, simply uploading software to a public repository does not necessarily mean that a project is ready for meaningful open source collaboration.

A well-prepared open source project generally needs appropriate licensing, clear documentation and enough structure for other users or developers to understand how the project works and how they can engage with it.

That is the gap this partnership is intended to address.

Learn more HERE

What Types of Projects Can Participate?

The program is designed for nonprofits with an existing technology project that is ready to be open sourced or that needs support to contribute to an existing open source project.

A nonprofit may therefore consider applying if it has:

  • An existing software tool it wants to make open source
  • A technology project that needs improved documentation
  • A software project that needs preparation for public release
  • An existing open source project that requires development support
  • A technical project that could benefit from a dedicated student development team

The organization should have a sufficiently defined project for the student developers and mentors to work on during the 16-week program.

Apply HERE

What Does the Nonprofit Need to Contribute?

Although the program is offered at no cost to participating organizations, selected nonprofits are expected to commit time and resources in the form of staff participation.

Each participating nonprofit should plan for approximately:

2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks

from a designated point-of-contact.

The nonprofit point-of-contact will participate in activities such as:

  • Regular check-ins
  • Providing feedback
  • Collaborating with student developers
  • Working with industry mentors
  • Answering project-related questions
  • Helping clarify priorities
  • Reviewing project progress
  • Supporting decision-making when necessary

This commitment is important because the student developers and mentors need a knowledgeable representative from the nonprofit to provide context and feedback.

How Much Time Should a Nonprofit Expect to Commit?

The stated commitment is approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks.

Over the entire program period, this represents approximately 32–48 hours of point-of-contact involvement.

Organizations should therefore select someone who can consistently participate throughout the program.

A nonprofit that cannot provide a reliable point-of-contact may struggle to take full advantage of the technical resources being provided.

What Does the Program Cost?

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offered at no cost to participating organizations.

This is one of the program’s major advantages because nonprofits can receive substantial technical support without having to pay for a professional software development team.

The program combines volunteer student developers with industry mentors and structured organizational support to provide the technical capacity needed to advance participating projects.

Why Open Source Can Matter for Nonprofits

Transforming nonprofit software into open source can have benefits beyond the immediate project.

A well-documented and publicly accessible tool can potentially:

  • Allow other nonprofits to use the technology.
  • Encourage collaboration among developers.
  • Reduce duplication of technology development.
  • Create opportunities for external contributions.
  • Increase the visibility of the organization’s technical work.
  • Make the software easier for other organizations to evaluate and adopt.
  • Build a community around a useful technology project.
  • Extend the impact of technology developed for a specific nonprofit mission.

The potential impact depends on the quality of the project, the needs of the wider community and the nonprofit’s ability to maintain and support the software after the program concludes.

Program Timeline

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership has a defined timeline from application through final delivery.

September 9, 2026 — Applications Close

This is the deadline for nonprofit organizations to submit their applications.

Organizations interested in participating should complete their application before this date.

October 2, 2026 — Selected Nonprofits Notified

Organizations selected to participate will be notified on this date.

October 25, 2026 — Program Kickoff

The program officially begins with the kickoff on October 25, 2026.

This marks the beginning of the 16-week collaboration involving the nonprofit, student developers and mentors.

February 20, 2027 — Final Delivery

The program is scheduled to conclude with final delivery on February 20, 2027.

By this stage, participating teams will have worked toward completing the agreed project objectives.

How to Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership

Nonprofit organizations interested in participating should submit an application through the program’s online application form.

Application deadline: September 9, 2026.

Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership

Before applying, organizations should make sure they understand the program requirements and can commit the necessary staff time for the entire 16-week period.

How Nonprofits Can Prepare a Strong Application

Although the provided information does not specify a detailed scoring rubric, organizations can prepare by clearly defining the project they want the program to support.

1. Identify the technology project

Determine which existing tool or project you want the student development team to work on.

The project should be sufficiently defined to explain what the team will be expected to accomplish.

2. Explain why the project should become open source

Organizations should be prepared to explain the value of making their technology publicly accessible.

Consider:

  • Who could benefit from the software?
  • What problem does the tool solve?
  • Why would other organizations use it?
  • What could an open source community contribute?
  • How could open sourcing the project increase its impact?

3. Define the technical challenges

Identify the areas where your organization needs support.

These could include:

  • Software development
  • Documentation
  • Open source preparation
  • Technical improvements
  • Contribution workflows
  • Existing open source development

A clear understanding of the project’s technical needs can help the development team work more effectively.

4. Identify a reliable point-of-contact

Choose a staff member or representative who can commit 2–3 hours each week for 16 weeks.

The person should have enough knowledge of the project to answer questions and provide meaningful feedback.

5. Consider the project’s sustainability

Open sourcing a project is not necessarily the end of the work.

Organizations should consider how the software will be maintained, documented and supported after the partnership ends.

Thinking about sustainability in advance can help ensure that the project’s results remain useful after February 2027.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is especially relevant to nonprofit organizations that have an existing technology or software project and want technical assistance to make it open source or contribute to an existing open source project.

A strong potential applicant may be a nonprofit that:

  • Has already built a software tool.
  • Has an existing technology project.
  • Wants to release its software as open source.
  • Needs assistance with documentation.
  • Wants to improve an existing open source project.
  • Has limited internal technical capacity.
  • Can provide a dedicated point-of-contact.
  • Can commit 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks.
  • Is prepared to collaborate closely with student developers and mentors.

What the Program Does Not Provide

Applicants should also understand the nature of the opportunity.

This is not described as a cash grant or direct financial award to nonprofits.

Instead, the core support comes in the form of:

  • Volunteer software development
  • Technical assistance
  • Open source guidance
  • Industry mentorship
  • Project management support
  • Team coaching
  • A structured 16-week development engagement

The primary value is therefore technical capacity and expertise rather than direct funding.

Questions to Ask Before Applying

Before submitting an application, a nonprofit should consider:

  1. Do we have an existing technology project?
  2. Is the project suitable for open source development?
  3. Are we prepared to make the project publicly accessible?
  4. Do we have a clear understanding of what technical work is required?
  5. Can we identify a point-of-contact?
  6. Can that person commit 2–3 hours every week for 16 weeks?
  7. Can our organization provide timely feedback to developers?
  8. Are we prepared to work collaboratively with college student developers?
  9. Can we engage with industry mentors?
  10. Do we have a plan for using or maintaining the project’s output after the program concludes?

If the answer to these questions is generally yes, the partnership may be worth considering.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership?

It is a collaborative program involving Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward that provides selected nonprofits with technical assistance to turn an existing software tool into an open source project or contribute to an existing open source project.

How many student developers does each nonprofit receive?

Each participating nonprofit receives a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers.

How long does the program last?

The program runs for 16 weeks.

How much technical work is provided?

Each team is expected to contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work.

Does the program charge participating nonprofits?

No. The opportunity is provided at no cost to participating nonprofits.

How much time must the nonprofit contribute?

The nonprofit’s designated point-of-contact should expect to contribute approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks.

What will the nonprofit representative do?

The point-of-contact will participate in check-ins, provide feedback and collaborate with student developers and industry mentors.

Does the program help with open source best practices?

Yes. CodeDay provides guidance on open source best practices.

Will nonprofits receive professional mentorship?

Yes. Experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers provide weekly guidance throughout the program.

What happens at the end of the program?

The program is scheduled to have its final delivery on February 20, 2027.

The intended outcome is a publicly accessible, licensed and documented project that the nonprofit can use and that may potentially be useful to other organizations.

When is the application deadline?

The nonprofit application deadline is September 9, 2026.

How do I apply?

Applications are submitted through the online application form:

Nonprofit Open Source Partnership application form

Contact Information

Organizations with questions about the program can contact:

Michael Gabrielle
Nonprofit Partnerships Manager
Develop for Good

Email: michael@developforgood.org

Important Dates to Remember

For convenience, applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

Date Milestone
September 9, 2026 Nonprofit applications close
October 2, 2026 Selected nonprofits notified
October 25, 2026 Program kickoff
February 20, 2027 Final delivery

The most immediate date for prospective applicants is September 9, 2026, which is the application deadline.

Conclusion

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership provides selected nonprofits with an opportunity to access significant technical development capacity without paying for it. Through a collaboration involving Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward, participating organizations can receive a dedicated team of eight college student developers, industry mentorship, open source guidance and structured project support.

The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have already developed a software tool but lack the internal time or technical capacity needed to properly prepare it for open source use. Rather than simply publishing existing code, participating teams can work toward creating a project that is publicly accessible, appropriately licensed and documented for future use.

The commitment from nonprofits is also clearly defined. Each organization should provide a point-of-contact who can dedicate approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks to check-ins, feedback and collaboration. This involvement will be important for ensuring that student developers understand the organization’s mission, users and technical priorities.

With applications closing on September 9, 2026, eligible nonprofits should begin identifying a suitable project, establishing their technical needs and selecting a reliable point-of-contact as soon as possible.

For nonprofits looking to expand the impact of their technology, improve an existing open source project or make an internally developed tool available to a wider community, this partnership offers an opportunity to gain technical expertise and development support without direct program costs.

Application deadline: September 9, 2026

item.content:encoded:
The KAUST Scholarship 2027 offers an exciting opportunity for international students seeking to pursue fully funded graduate studies at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) in Saudi Arabia. The scholarship is available for students applying to eligible Master’s and PhD degree programs beginning in Spring 2027. Designed to support talented students pursuing advanced study and research, the KAUST scholarship provides comprehensive financial assistance, including tuition coverage, a monthly living stipend, accommodation, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support for international students. Applications for the Spring 2027 intake are currently open, and prospective applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their documents well before the deadline.

Application deadline: September 27, 2026.

KAUST Scholarship 2027 Overview

The KAUST Scholarship provides international graduate students with the opportunity to study at a research-intensive university in Saudi Arabia while undertaking advanced work in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and related research areas.

Here are the key details:

  • University: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
  • Location: Saudi Arabia
  • Study level: Master’s and PhD
  • Intake: Spring 2027
  • Duration: Approximately 2 years for Master’s programs and 3–4 years for doctoral programs
  • Funding: Fully funded
  • Tuition: Fully covered
  • Monthly stipend: Provided
  • Accommodation: On-campus housing provided
  • Medical coverage: Included
  • Dental coverage: Included
  • Relocation support: Available for international students
  • Eligible applicants: International students from around the world
  • Application deadline: September 27, 2026
  • Application method: Online

About King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) was established in 2009 and has developed into a major research-focused university in Saudi Arabia.

The university places a strong emphasis on scientific research, innovation, technology and graduate education. Its academic environment is particularly focused on research areas associated with science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

KAUST’s research-oriented model makes it an attractive destination for students interested in developing advanced technical knowledge and contributing to research addressing scientific and technological challenges.

The university has also received international recognition for its research output. According to the information provided for this opportunity, KAUST was ranked 19th globally in the 2016 Nature Index Rising Stars recognition of universities experiencing rapid growth in high-quality research output and scientific publications.

What Is the KAUST Scholarship 2027?

The KAUST Scholarship is a comprehensive financial support package associated with admission to eligible graduate programs at KAUST.

Rather than requiring students to independently secure separate funding for tuition and living costs, admitted students are automatically considered for the scholarship according to the information provided.

This means that qualified applicants who are admitted to an eligible program can receive substantial financial support throughout their studies.

The scholarship is intended to allow graduate students to focus on their education and research without carrying the typical financial burden associated with international graduate study.

Master’s Programs at KAUST

The scholarship is available to students pursuing eligible Master’s degree programs.

The expected duration for Master’s studies is approximately two years.

During this period, students can undertake graduate-level coursework and research while becoming part of KAUST’s international academic and research community.

Students interested in Master’s study should carefully examine the specific admission requirements of their intended program because meeting the general scholarship conditions does not replace the academic requirements for admission.

PhD Programs at KAUST

The opportunity is also available to students seeking doctoral study.

KAUST’s PhD programs are research-intensive and generally require approximately three to four years, depending on the program, research requirements and individual academic progress.

Doctoral students can use their time at KAUST to develop specialised expertise, conduct original research and contribute to scientific knowledge in their chosen area.

Prospective PhD applicants should pay particular attention to identifying an appropriate research direction and demonstrating their academic and research preparation in their application.

Available Fields and Majors

The KAUST Scholarship is available across the academic subjects and research areas offered by the university.

The institution has a strong focus on:

  • Science
  • Technology
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics
  • Scientific research
  • Advanced technological research
  • Related interdisciplinary fields

Because the scholarship is tied to admission to KAUST graduate programs, applicants should review the programs currently offered by the university and select a field that matches their academic background, research interests and career objectives.

Applicants should also ensure that their previous academic qualifications satisfy the entry requirements of the specific program they select.

Financial Benefits of the KAUST Scholarship

One of the most significant features of the KAUST Scholarship is its comprehensive funding package.

According to the information provided, successful students can receive the following benefits.

1. Full Tuition Fee Coverage

The scholarship covers the student’s tuition fees for the eligible graduate program.

This can significantly reduce the financial cost of obtaining a Master’s or PhD degree abroad.

2. Monthly Living Stipend

Students receive a monthly stipend intended to help cover living expenses while studying at KAUST.

The stipend allows students to concentrate more fully on their studies and research without having to finance their everyday expenses entirely from personal savings.

3. On-Campus Accommodation

The scholarship includes access to on-campus housing accommodation.

This is particularly useful for international students relocating to Saudi Arabia because it reduces the difficulty and expense associated with finding private accommodation after arrival.

4. Medical Coverage

The financial package includes medical coverage, providing students with access to healthcare support during their studies.

5. Dental Coverage

Dental coverage is also included as part of the scholarship’s comprehensive support package.

6. Relocation Support

International students may receive relocation support, helping them manage some of the costs and practical challenges associated with moving to Saudi Arabia for their studies.

Taken together, these benefits make the opportunity particularly attractive to students who would otherwise find the cost of international graduate education difficult to manage.

Duration of the KAUST Scholarship

The expected duration depends on the level of study.

Master’s degree

The Master’s scholarship support is generally provided for approximately:

2 years

PhD degree

Doctoral scholarship support is generally provided for approximately:

3–4 years

The actual period of study and funding may depend on the student’s program, academic progress and applicable university requirements.

KAUST Scholarship Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy the admission requirements for the Master’s or PhD program they intend to study.

The provided requirements include the following:

  • Applicants must meet the entry requirements for their selected graduate program.
  • International students from any country can apply.
  • Applicants should be seeking admission for the Spring 2027 intake.
  • Applicants must satisfy the applicable English-language requirements unless exempt.
  • Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation.
  • GRE scores are not mandatory, although they may strengthen an application when available.

Because admission requirements can differ between programs, applicants should not rely exclusively on the general scholarship requirements. They should also review the requirements for their chosen KAUST degree program.

English Language Requirements

English-language proficiency is an important part of the application.

The information provided lists the following minimum scores:

  • TOEFL iBT: 79
  • IELTS: 6.0

Applicants should make sure that their test results satisfy the university’s applicable requirements before submitting their application.

Who may be exempt from English-language test requirements?

According to the provided information, TOEFL or IELTS scores are not required if the applicant received their degree from an accredited institution in one of the following countries:

  • United States
  • Canada
  • United Kingdom
  • Ireland
  • Australia
  • New Zealand

Applicants should nevertheless verify their individual circumstances and the current requirements applicable to their program before submitting the application.

Letters of Recommendation

Applicants are required to submit three letters of recommendation.

Recommendation letters can provide admissions reviewers with independent evidence of an applicant’s academic ability, research potential, intellectual maturity and suitability for graduate-level study.

Applicants should therefore select recommenders who know their academic or research work well and can provide specific, meaningful assessments of their abilities.

Where possible, applicants should approach potential referees well in advance of the application deadline.

Is the GRE Required?

The GRE is not mandatory according to the information provided.

However, GRE scores may be considered advantageous if an applicant has them available.

Applicants should therefore avoid delaying their application solely because they have not taken the GRE, while also considering whether submitting a valid score could strengthen their particular application.

Required Documents for the KAUST Scholarship

Prospective applicants should prepare the required documentation before beginning or completing their online application.

The provided list includes:

Academic Transcript

Applicants should submit their academic transcript.

The transcript must be presented in English.

It should accurately demonstrate the applicant’s academic history and qualifications.

Degree Certificate

A degree certificate is also required and should be presented in English.

Applicants should make sure that their submitted documents clearly demonstrate completion of their previous degree.

IELTS or English-Language Test Result

Applicants who are required to demonstrate English proficiency should prepare a valid IELTS or TOEFL result according to the university’s requirements.

Applicants from non-English-speaking countries should pay particular attention to this requirement.

However, the provided information indicates that applicants who received their degree from accredited institutions in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand are exempt from submitting TOEFL or IELTS scores.

Three Recommendation Letters

Applicants must provide:

Three letters of recommendation.

These should ideally come from individuals who can provide credible information about the applicant’s academic and research capabilities.

Current CV or Resume

A current curriculum vitae or resume should be included.

The CV should present the applicant’s academic background, research experience, publications, projects, awards, professional experience and other relevant achievements.

Valid Passport

International applicants should provide a valid passport.

Applicants should check the validity of their passport before submitting their application, particularly because an international move may require sufficient passport validity for visa and travel arrangements.

Passport-Size Photograph

A current passport-size photograph is also listed among the required documents.

Research Articles

Research articles may be included if available.

For research-focused Master’s and PhD applicants, publications or other evidence of research experience can help demonstrate preparation for graduate-level study.

Automatic Scholarship Consideration for Admitted Students

A notable feature of the opportunity is that, according to the provided information, all admitted students automatically receive the scholarship.

This means applicants do not need to compete for a limited number of separate scholarship awards after admission in the manner common to many external funding programs.

Instead, the scholarship is associated with admission to the eligible graduate program.

This makes the academic admission application especially important. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a strong overall application that demonstrates their academic qualifications, research potential and suitability for their chosen program.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The KAUST Scholarship may be particularly relevant to students who:

  • Want to pursue a Master’s degree in a research-focused environment.
  • Are interested in pursuing a PhD abroad.
  • Have strong academic qualifications.
  • Want to develop advanced expertise in science, technology, engineering or mathematics.
  • Are interested in scientific research and innovation.
  • Need comprehensive financial support for graduate education.
  • Are prepared to relocate to Saudi Arabia.
  • Have research interests compatible with KAUST’s academic programs.
  • Meet the English-language requirements or qualify for an exemption.
  • Can provide three strong recommendation letters.
  • Are preparing for the Spring 2027 intake.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Meeting the minimum requirements does not necessarily guarantee admission. Prospective applicants should use the application to demonstrate why they are a strong fit for their chosen program.

1. Choose the right program

Start by identifying the KAUST graduate program that best matches your previous degree, research interests and long-term goals.

Your academic background should make sense in relation to the program you select.

2. Research the academic environment

Applicants should investigate the university’s research areas and identify the areas that align most closely with their interests.

This can help candidates develop a more focused application.

3. Prepare your academic documents early

Do not wait until shortly before the deadline to request transcripts, degree certificates and recommendation letters.

International applicants may need additional time to obtain official documents or translations.

4. Prepare your CV carefully

Your CV should clearly communicate your academic and research achievements.

Where applicable, include:

  • Research projects
  • Publications
  • Conference participation
  • Academic awards
  • Research experience
  • Internships
  • Relevant employment
  • Technical skills
  • Laboratory experience
  • Academic achievements

5. Secure strong recommendation letters

Contact your referees early and provide them with enough information about the program and your academic goals.

This gives them an opportunity to prepare detailed and relevant recommendations.

6. Check your English-language status

Determine whether you need IELTS or TOEFL before submitting the application.

If you are required to provide a test score, make sure your result meets the stated minimum.

7. Apply before the deadline

Do not leave the application until the final day.

Technical issues, missing documents or problems uploading files can prevent an otherwise qualified applicant from completing the application successfully.

Application Deadline for KAUST Scholarship 2027

The stated deadline for the Spring 2027 KAUST Scholarship is:

September 27, 2026.

Prospective applicants should ensure that all required application components are completed and submitted before the stated deadline.

Since the deadline is approaching, applicants should begin gathering documents, contacting referees and reviewing program-specific admission requirements as early as possible.

How to Apply for the KAUST Scholarship 2027

The application process is conducted entirely online.

Applicants should begin by reviewing the available graduate programs and identifying the program that best fits their academic and research background.

The general process involves:

  1. Review KAUST’s Master’s and PhD programs.
  2. Select the degree and academic area that matches your interests.
  3. Review the admission requirements for the selected program.
  4. Prepare your academic transcripts and degree certificates.
  5. Prepare your CV or resume.
  6. Arrange three recommendation letters.
  7. Prepare your valid passport and passport-size photograph.
  8. Prepare an English-language test result if required.
  9. Include research articles or other relevant research evidence if available.
  10. Complete the online application.
  11. Upload the required supporting documents.
  12. Review the application carefully.
  13. Submit the application before September 27, 2026.

Applicants should use the official KAUST application portal and consult the university’s current instructions for the latest program-specific requirements.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before submitting an application, prospective students should keep several points in mind.

First, being an international applicant does not by itself guarantee admission. Candidates must still satisfy the admission requirements for their chosen Master’s or PhD program.

Second, the scholarship is described as being automatically awarded to admitted students, making the overall academic application extremely important.

Third, applicants should pay attention to English-language requirements. While the provided information lists TOEFL iBT 79 and IELTS 6.0 as minimum scores, certain applicants may be exempt based on where they obtained their previous degree.

Fourth, recommendation letters are a required component of the application. Candidates should not wait until the final days before contacting potential referees.

Finally, applicants should check all documents carefully before submission to ensure that the application is complete.

Frequently Asked Questions About the KAUST Scholarship 2027

Is the KAUST Scholarship fully funded?

Yes. The opportunity is described as a fully funded scholarship providing comprehensive financial support, including tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support for international students.

Who can apply for the KAUST Scholarship?

International students from any country can apply, provided they meet the admission requirements for their selected Master’s or PhD program.

What degree levels are covered?

The opportunity covers eligible Master’s and PhD programs.

When does the 2027 scholarship begin?

The provided opportunity is for students beginning their studies in Spring 2027.

What is the application deadline?

The stated deadline is September 27, 2026.

How long does the Master’s program take?

The provided information states that Master’s programs are generally supported for approximately two years.

How long does the PhD program take?

Doctoral programs are generally expected to take approximately three to four years, depending on the program and academic progress.

Do I need IELTS?

Applicants generally need to meet the stated English-language requirement unless they qualify for an exemption.

The provided minimum scores are IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 79.

Is the GRE compulsory?

No. The GRE is not mandatory according to the provided information, although a score may be advantageous if available.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Applicants must submit three letters of recommendation.

Do all admitted students receive the scholarship?

According to the information provided, all admitted students automatically receive the scholarship.

Can applicants from outside Saudi Arabia apply?

Yes. The opportunity is specifically open to international students from countries around the world.

Where will students study?

Successful applicants will study at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Saudi Arabia.

Learn more HERE

Final Checklist for Applicants

Before submitting your application, make sure you have considered the following:

  • Confirm that you meet the entry requirements for your selected program.
  • Confirm that your academic background matches the program.
  • Check the applicable English-language requirements.
  • Determine whether you qualify for an English-language test exemption.
  • Prepare your academic transcript in English.
  • Prepare your degree certificate in English.
  • Prepare your current CV or resume.
  • Obtain three recommendation letters.
  • Prepare a valid passport.
  • Prepare a passport-size photograph.
  • Include research articles if available.
  • Review your selected program carefully.
  • Check the application for missing information.
  • Submit the application online before the deadline.
  • Keep a copy of your submitted application and supporting documents.

Financial Support​

All admitted students receive the benefits of the KAUST Fellowship which supports students for the duration of their graduate studies. The benefits of the KAUST Fellowship include:

  • ​Full tuition support
  • Monthly living allowance (ranging between $20,000-30,000 annually, depending on qualifications and progression through degree programs)
  • Housing*
  • Medical and dental coverage*
  • Relocation support

* Charges may apply to dependent housing and medical and dental coverage.

Conclusion

The KAUST Scholarship 2027 is a significant opportunity for international students seeking fully funded Master’s or PhD study in Saudi Arabia. Through comprehensive financial support, the program is designed to allow admitted graduate students to concentrate on their academic development and research while studying at a research-intensive university.

The funding package includes full tuition coverage, a monthly living stipend, on-campus accommodation, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support for international students, making it an attractive option for students who want to pursue advanced education without the substantial financial burden normally associated with international graduate study.

The opportunity is open to international students from any country, while applicants must still satisfy the admission requirements of their chosen KAUST program. Candidates should also pay close attention to English-language requirements, recommendation letters and supporting documentation.

For students interested in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and related research areas, KAUST can provide an international research environment in which to develop advanced knowledge and contribute to scientific innovation.

The Spring 2027 application deadline is September 27, 2026. Prospective applicants should begin preparing their documents and reviewing their chosen program as early as possible to ensure that they can submit a complete and competitive application before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Young researchers from South Asia have an opportunity to advance their academic careers, strengthen international research networks and develop collaborative research projects through the Joint Scholarship Programme of the South Asia Institute (SAI), Heidelberg University, and the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies Delhi (MWF Delhi).

The programme is inviting applications for a three-month research fellowship in Heidelberg, Germany, during summer 2027. The opportunity is designed for promising young scholars from selected South Asian countries who want to establish or deepen research collaboration with the South Asia Institute at Heidelberg University.

Successful fellows will spend up to three months at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg, where they will work on a research project previously outlined in their application. An important component of the fellowship is the development of the research project into a potential third-party funding application, which could seek support for future research, academic exchanges or scientific events.

The programme therefore offers more than a short-term research stay. It provides an opportunity for early-career researchers to gain international academic exposure, build institutional connections, participate in scholarly activities and potentially develop their research into a larger externally funded project.

Heidelberg University South Asia Joint Scholarship Programme 2027

The fellowship is being offered by the South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University in cooperation with the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies Delhi.

The programme is particularly intended to facilitate research collaboration between young scholars from South Asia and researchers at the South Asia Institute. Applicants are expected to propose a clearly defined research project that can be further developed during their stay in Heidelberg.

The fellowship is scheduled to begin sometime between April and June 2027 and will run for approximately three months.

During the fellowship period, the successful candidate’s place of residence will be Heidelberg, Germany.

What Does the Fellowship Offer?

The Joint Scholarship Programme provides financial and academic support to selected researchers during their stay in Heidelberg.

The fellowship package includes several important forms of support:

1. Monthly Scholarship of EUR 1,200

Successful fellows will receive a monthly scholarship instalment of EUR 1,200 during the fellowship period.

This financial support is intended to assist fellows with living expenses while undertaking their research stay in Heidelberg.

2. International Travel Support of Up to EUR 1,500

The programme also provides reimbursement of international travel expenses of up to EUR 1,500.

This can help reduce the financial burden associated with travelling to and from Germany for the research fellowship.

3. Rental Cost Support

The fellowship also includes payment of rental costs, providing additional assistance with accommodation expenses during the research stay in Heidelberg.

Together, the monthly scholarship, travel reimbursement and rental-cost support make the programme a significant opportunity for researchers seeking international academic experience without having to bear the full cost of a research stay abroad.

Duration and Location of the Fellowship

The fellowship will last for three months.

The programme is expected to begin between April and June 2027, meaning successful applicants will undertake their research stay during the summer period of 2027.

The fellowship will be based at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg, with Heidelberg serving as the fellow’s place of residence during the programme.

Researchers should therefore be prepared to spend the fellowship period in Germany and actively engage with the academic environment at the South Asia Institute.

Research Areas Covered by the Programme

The programme is particularly interested in applications connected to a broad range of disciplines relating to South Asia.

Applicants working in the following areas are specifically encouraged to apply:

  • Ethnology
  • History
  • Political science
  • Economics
  • Geography
  • Modern languages and literatures of South Asia
  • Cultural history of South Asia
  • Religious history of South Asia
  • Classical Indology

The multidisciplinary nature of the programme means that researchers can approach South Asian studies from different academic perspectives.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed project is academically relevant to the areas supported by the programme and that the research can benefit from collaboration with the South Asia Institute.

What Will Fellows Do During the Three-Month Research Stay?

The fellowship is structured around a research project that applicants must already define as part of their application.

During their time at the South Asia Institute, fellows will be expected to take the proposed project forward and develop it further.

A major objective is to transform the initial research project into a potential third-party funding application.

This could involve seeking future funding for:

  • Research projects
  • Academic exchange programmes
  • Scientific events
  • Collaborative research initiatives
  • Other relevant academic activities

This component makes the fellowship particularly valuable for researchers who want to move beyond an individual research project and develop longer-term academic collaborations and externally funded research opportunities.

Participation in Academic Events

Fellows will also be expected to actively participate in scientific events at the South Asia Institute during their stay.

This requirement provides an opportunity for researchers to interact with scholars, exchange ideas and become part of the academic environment at the institute.

Participation in scientific activities can also help fellows:

  • Expand their academic networks.
  • Exchange knowledge with researchers working in related disciplines.
  • Present or discuss research ideas.
  • Identify potential research collaborators.
  • Gain exposure to international academic practices.
  • Develop relationships that could continue after the fellowship.
  • Explore future opportunities for joint research and funding.

For young scholars seeking to establish an international research profile, this networking component can be an important part of the fellowship experience.

Who Can Apply for the Heidelberg University South Asia Fellowship?

The programme is specifically aimed at young researchers from South Asia.

Applicants must be from one of the five countries identified by the programme:

  1. India
  2. Nepal
  3. Pakistan
  4. Sri Lanka
  5. Bangladesh

The programme is therefore geographically focused on South Asia rather than being open to applicants from every country worldwide.

Researchers from other countries who do not meet the programme’s geographic eligibility requirements should not assume that they qualify based on academic qualifications alone.

Academic Qualification Required

Applicants are required to provide a copy of their doctoral certificate as part of the application documents.

This means the opportunity is intended for researchers who have completed doctoral-level studies and can demonstrate this through their doctoral certificate.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they meet the programme’s academic requirements before beginning the application process.

Application Documents Required

Applicants must submit their materials through the online application system.

The application requires several documents, which should be carefully prepared before submission.

1. Online Application Form

Applicants must complete the official online application form.

The form is the primary method through which applications are submitted to the programme.

2. Short Cover Letter

Applicants must submit a short cover letter of no more than one page.

The cover letter should clearly communicate the applicant’s motivation for applying and explain why the fellowship and proposed research collaboration are relevant to their academic development.

Because the cover letter is limited to one page, applicants should focus on the most important information rather than providing a lengthy academic biography.

3. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a curriculum vitae of no more than two pages.

The CV should include the applicant’s top ten publications.

Researchers should therefore prioritise their strongest and most relevant academic publications rather than attempting to provide an exhaustive publication history.

4. Doctoral Certificate

A copy of the applicant’s doctoral certificate must be included.

Applicants should ensure that the submitted document is clear and readable.

5. Project Description

Applicants must prepare a project description using the designated project-description template.

The template must be downloaded, completed with the required information and uploaded together with the other application documents.

The project description is particularly important because the fellowship is built around developing the proposed research project during the three-month stay.

Applicants should therefore present a clear, academically sound and achievable research proposal.

6. List of Two Referees

Applicants must provide a list of two referees who may be contacted later to provide additional information about the applicant.

Applicants should select referees who can credibly comment on their academic background, research abilities and potential.

7. Letter of Reference from an SAI Member

A letter of reference from a member of the South Asia Institute is optional.

Although it is not listed as a mandatory requirement, applicants who have an established academic connection with an SAI member may consider whether obtaining such a reference would strengthen their application.

Important Application Document Requirement

One important instruction is that the application documents must be uploaded as a single PDF.

Applicants should therefore combine the required attachments into one PDF document before submitting the application.

The application package should contain the relevant documents, including:

  • Cover letter
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Doctoral certificate
  • Project description
  • List of two referees
  • Optional SAI member reference letter

Applicants should carefully check the document requirements before submitting the application to avoid omissions.

Heidelberg University Fellowship Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline.

It is advisable not to wait until the final hours of the application period, particularly because applicants need to prepare several documents and combine the required attachments into a single PDF.

The selection process is expected to take place by the end of 2026.

How to Apply for the South Asia Institute Joint Scholarship Programme

Applications must be submitted online through the official application portal.

The programme explicitly states that applications sent by email will not be considered.

Applicants should therefore follow these steps:

Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements

Confirm that you are a young researcher from one of the eligible South Asian countries and that you meet the academic requirements.

Step 2: Develop Your Research Project

Prepare a well-defined research project that can be undertaken and further developed during the three-month stay at the South Asia Institute.

The project should have clear academic value and potential for future development into a third-party funding application.

Step 3: Prepare the Cover Letter

Write a concise cover letter of no more than one page explaining your motivation, research interests and the relevance of the fellowship to your academic development.

Step 4: Update Your CV

Prepare a maximum two-page academic CV and include your top ten publications.

Step 5: Complete the Project Description Template

Download and complete the required project-description template.

Applicants should ensure that all requested information is properly addressed.

Step 6: Identify Two Referees

Prepare a list of two referees who may be contacted to provide additional information about your academic and research background.

Step 7: Add Supporting Documents

Include a copy of your doctoral certificate and, where applicable, an optional letter of reference from an SAI member.

Step 8: Combine the Documents into One PDF

The application attachments should be uploaded as a single PDF.

Check the document carefully before submission to ensure that all required materials are included and legible.

Step 9: Submit Through the Online Portal

Complete the online application and upload the required PDF through the designated application portal.

Applications sent by email will not be considered.

APPLY HERE

Visa Assistance for Successful Applicants

The programme also provides support for applicants who may require assistance with visa-related arrangements.

The SAI Delhi office will provide assistance with visa applications if necessary.

This is an important consideration for successful applicants who need to obtain the appropriate documentation to travel to Germany for their fellowship.

Applicants should nevertheless make sure that they understand the applicable visa requirements and follow the instructions provided by the programme after selection.

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Young Researchers

The Heidelberg University and Max Weber Forum joint fellowship offers several potential benefits for researchers at the early stages of their academic careers.

International Research Experience

Spending three months at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg gives fellows the opportunity to work within an international academic environment.

Academic Networking

Active participation in scientific events can enable fellows to connect with researchers and academics whose interests overlap with their own.

Research Collaboration

The programme specifically seeks to establish and develop research collaboration between young scholars from South Asia and the South Asia Institute.

Funding Development Skills

A particularly important feature of the fellowship is the opportunity to develop the research project into a third-party funding application.

This can help researchers gain practical experience in developing projects suitable for future external funding.

Financial Support

The programme provides a monthly scholarship of EUR 1,200, international travel reimbursement of up to EUR 1,500, and payment of rental costs.

Exposure to Heidelberg’s Academic Environment

The fellowship provides an opportunity to conduct research while being based at Heidelberg University’s South Asia Institute in Germany.

Potential Long-Term Academic Opportunities

The relationships established during the fellowship could potentially support future research partnerships, academic exchanges, events and funding applications.

Visit HERE for more information about the Heidelberg University Joint Scholarship Programme 2027.

What Makes the Programme Different?

Unlike an opportunity focused exclusively on financial assistance, this fellowship combines funding, international research experience, academic networking and project development.

The requirement to develop the proposed project into a potential third-party funding application means fellows are expected to think beyond the three-month fellowship.

The programme can therefore serve as a platform for researchers who want to develop a longer-term research agenda and build institutional relationships with scholars at the South Asia Institute.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants interested in this fellowship should pay close attention to the quality and relevance of their application.

Make the Research Project Clear

The proposed research should be clearly defined and demonstrate why the project would benefit from being developed at the South Asia Institute.

Demonstrate Academic Strength

The CV should highlight the applicant’s strongest academic achievements, research experience and top publications.

Explain the Value of Collaboration

Applicants should clearly communicate why collaboration with the South Asia Institute is important for their research and how the fellowship could strengthen their work.

Connect the Project to Future Funding

Since the programme expects the research project to be developed into a third-party funding application, applicants should consider how the proposed research could eventually evolve into a larger externally funded initiative.

Follow Every Formatting Requirement

Applicants should respect the limits of the following:

  • One page for the cover letter.
  • Two pages for the CV.
  • One PDF for the application attachments.

Failure to follow instructions can make an otherwise strong application unnecessarily difficult to assess.

Submit Before the Deadline

The final deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET. Applicants should allow sufficient time to complete the online form and upload their documents.

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity Joint Scholarship Programme of the South Asia Institute, Heidelberg University and Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies Delhi
Fellowship duration Three months
Programme period April–June 2027 start window
Location Heidelberg, Germany
Target group Young researchers from South Asia
Eligible countries India, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh
Academic requirement Doctoral qualification; doctoral certificate required
Monthly scholarship EUR 1,200
International travel support Up to EUR 1,500
Accommodation support Rental costs covered
Research focus South Asian studies and related disciplines
Application method Online
Application attachments One combined PDF
Cover letter Maximum 1 page
CV Maximum 2 pages, including top ten publications
Referees Two referees
SAI reference Optional
Application deadline 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
Selection By the end of 2026

Final Thoughts

The Joint Scholarship Programme of the South Asia Institute, Heidelberg University and the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies, Delhi, provides a valuable international research opportunity for young scholars from India, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

With a three-month research stay in Heidelberg, a EUR 1,200 monthly scholarship, international travel support of up to EUR 1,500, rental-cost support and opportunities to participate in academic activities, the fellowship can provide both financial assistance and meaningful professional development.

Perhaps most importantly, the programme is designed to encourage researchers to turn an initial research idea into a potentially larger project capable of attracting third-party funding. This makes it particularly relevant to doctoral-level researchers seeking to expand their academic networks, strengthen research collaborations and develop sustainable international research initiatives.

Eligible researchers who are interested in South Asian studies and related disciplines should carefully prepare their application materials and submit their applications through the official online portal before 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Applicants should also remember that email applications will not be considered, and the required supporting documents must be uploaded as a single PDF through the online application system.
