item.content:encoded:
The MATS Residency Winter 2027 is inviting talented individuals from around the world to apply for its upcoming intake, offering an opportunity to pursue ambitious research and safety-relevant projects focused on reducing catastrophic risks from advanced artificial intelligence.

The Residency is designed for people who can demonstrate strong research ability and the potential to produce meaningful work in AI safety. Importantly, applicants are not required to have a PhD, a formal “researcher” job title, an extensive publication record, or previous AI safety experience.

The Winter 2027 application window runs from 25 August to 31 October 2026, giving prospective applicants several weeks to prepare and submit their applications.

MATS Residency Winter 2027

The MATS Residency is intended to support individuals working on important questions surrounding AI alignment, AI safety, AI governance, evaluations, assurance and advanced AI systems.

Rather than relying primarily on conventional academic credentials, the program evaluates the quality, seriousness and potential impact of an applicant’s work.

This makes the Residency particularly relevant to talented researchers, technical professionals, policy experts, entrepreneurs and individuals transitioning into AI safety who can demonstrate that they have the ability to tackle difficult, open-ended problems.

The program is also internationally accessible. Applicants can express a preference for one of three office locations — London, Berkeley or Washington, DC — and the Residency provides visa support for participants who need to relocate internationally.

Apply for the MATS Residency Winter 2027

Opportunity Category

Category: Fellowship / Research Residency

The MATS Residency is a structured research program that supports participants in developing AI safety research, safety-relevant projects or incubation initiatives.

MATS Residency Winter 2027 Deadline

The application window for the Winter 2027 intake is:

Opening date: 25 August 2026
Application deadline: 31 October 2026
Deadline timezone: Anywhere on Earth (AoE)

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because the application requires several components, including references, a work sample and written responses.

The next application window after the Winter 2027 intake is scheduled to open in March 2027.

When Will Applicants Hear Back?

Applications are reviewed by the MATS Residency team, with input from program advisors where appropriate.

The expected selection timeline is:

  1. Applications close: 31 October 2026.
  2. Application review: Applications are assessed by the Residency team.
  3. Application outcome: Applicants are expected to hear about the outcome by the end of November 2026.
  4. Interviews or paid work tests: Shortlisted applicants may be invited to an interview or paid work test during the first week of December 2026, depending on their track and research area.
  5. Final selection: Selected Residents are expected to be informed by the end of 2026.
  6. Residency start: Successful applicants are expected to begin in early 2027.

Information about interviews and panel members will be provided to shortlisted applicants beforehand.

Who Should Apply for the MATS Residency?

One of the most important features of the MATS Residency is its approach to evaluating applicants.

The program emphasizes what an applicant can do and the quality of their work, rather than simply looking at conventional credentials.

You do not necessarily need:

  • A PhD.
  • A master’s degree in AI safety.
  • A job title containing the word “researcher.”
  • A long list of academic publications.
  • Previous professional experience specifically in AI safety.
  • A conventional academic research career.

The program is interested in talented individuals who can demonstrate the ability to produce outstanding AI safety research or safety-relevant work.

This can include people whose strongest work is:

  • Confidential.
  • Unpublished.
  • Conducted outside academia.
  • Completed as part of an industry team.
  • Based on technical or policy work.
  • Demonstrated through projects rather than traditional publications.

If an applicant is uncertain about whether their background qualifies, MATS encourages them to apply or contact the Residency team before submitting an application.

What Research Does MATS Want to Support?

Applicants are expected to submit a brief plan describing what they would like to accomplish during the Residency.

Depending on the chosen track, this may take the form of:

  • A research plan.
  • A plan for safety-relevant work.
  • A project plan.
  • A plan to build or test an idea.
  • A business or organizational plan for an incubation project.

The proposed work should explain its theory of change — in other words, how the proposed research or project could ultimately contribute to improving AI safety and reducing catastrophic risks associated with advanced AI.

1. Impact

MATS places significant emphasis on potentially high-impact work.

The Residency is particularly interested in ambitious, longer-term projects that may not fit neatly within conventional academic or industry structures.

Applicants should demonstrate why their proposed work could make a meaningful contribution to reducing catastrophic AI risk.

2. Depth

The program is interested in foundational questions that may require substantial time and sustained investigation.

Applicants should therefore think beyond projects that can be completed within a few weeks and instead consider research questions that could generate important insights over a longer period.

Priority AI Safety Research Areas

Although applicants are not restricted to a predetermined list of topics, MATS identifies several areas where it is particularly interested in supporting research.

Safe Automation of Alignment Research

One area of interest involves determining how AI systems can be used to accelerate alignment research while preserving meaningful human oversight.

As AI systems become increasingly capable, researchers face an important challenge: how can AI-assisted research remain checkable, reliable and subject to appropriate oversight?

Research in this area may explore methods for ensuring that AI systems assisting with alignment research do not make the research process impossible for humans to adequately evaluate.

Safety Cases, Evaluations, AI Strategy and AI Assurance

MATS is also interested in work involving:

  • AI safety cases.
  • AI evaluations.
  • AI strategy.
  • AI assurance.
  • Technical AI governance.

These areas focus on building stronger evidence, methodologies and frameworks that can help organizations and policymakers make informed decisions about advanced AI.

Research may contribute to ways of demonstrating that advanced AI systems meet particular safety requirements or establishing processes for evaluating their risks.

Agentic and Multi-Agent AI Safety

Another priority area concerns agentic and multi-agent AI systems.

As AI systems become capable of acting more autonomously and interacting with other AI agents, new safety and alignment challenges can emerge.

Research in this area may examine how autonomous systems should be designed, evaluated, monitored and aligned when they can independently pursue goals or interact with other systems.

Applicants Are Not Limited to the Priority Areas

The priority areas listed by MATS are intended to provide transparency about the research directions the program is particularly interested in supporting.

They are not intended to prevent applicants from proposing other important AI alignment or AI safety research.

Applicants should propose the work they genuinely believe is important and explain:

  • What problem they are trying to solve.
  • Why the problem matters.
  • What they intend to investigate.
  • How their proposed work could contribute to AI safety.
  • What evidence would demonstrate progress.
  • How the work could ultimately reduce catastrophic risks from AI.

A strong theory of change can therefore be an important component of a competitive application.

MATS Residency Office Locations

Applicants can indicate a preferred office location when applying.

The three locations are:

  • London
  • Berkeley
  • Washington, DC

The Residency follows a hybrid model.

Residents are expected to spend at least one-third of their Residency working in person from the program’s offices.

There is no requirement to remain permanently assigned to one particular office. Residents may spend their in-person time at different MATS offices and can move between locations during the program.

Applicants should therefore select the location that provides the strongest proximity to:

  • Relevant AI research laboratories.
  • Potential collaborators.
  • Researchers.
  • Technical communities.
  • Policy communities.
  • Other resources relevant to their proposed research.

If multiple locations would be equally suitable, applicants can indicate this in their application.

International Applicants

The MATS Residency is open to applicants internationally.

This is particularly important for researchers and professionals based outside the United States and United Kingdom.

For successful applicants who need to relocate internationally, MATS states that it provides visa support.

International applicants should nevertheless carefully consider their work-authorization circumstances and provide the required information in the application.

MATS Residency Application Requirements

Applicants must submit several components through the online application system.

Preparation is therefore important, particularly for applicants who need to contact referees or prepare a representative research sample.

1. Short Profile and Eligibility Section

Applicants begin by providing basic information for application processing and logistics.

This section includes information such as:

  • Contact details.
  • Current affiliation.
  • CV.
  • Preferred office.
  • Availability for the intake.
  • Work-authorization status.
  • Highest degree.
  • Previous MATS involvement.

The CV must be no longer than two pages.

According to MATS, this section is primarily used for routing and logistical purposes rather than being the central component of the assessment.

2. Track Choice

Applicants must select the MATS track that best fits their circumstances and proposed work.

They are also asked to provide a brief explanation of approximately two to three sentences explaining why the selected track is appropriate.

The track-selection explanation can help reviewers determine whether an applicant may be better suited to another pathway.

3. References

Applicants must provide two references who can directly speak to the quality of their work.

This is especially relevant for applicants whose strongest work is not publicly available.

For example, if an applicant has worked on confidential research or contributed to a larger team, their referee may be able to verify the applicant’s contribution.

Some tracks have additional requirements concerning referees, so applicants should carefully review the requirements for their chosen track.

4. Representative Work Sample

Applicants must submit one work sample that best demonstrates their strongest or most relevant work.

Possible examples include:

  • Academic papers.
  • Research reports.
  • Technical reports.
  • Software repositories.
  • Evaluations.
  • Policy analyses.
  • Other substantial research outputs.

The strongest submission is not necessarily the most prestigious document. Applicants should select the work that best demonstrates their ability to conduct rigorous, valuable and independent work.

5. Written Responses

Applicants must complete:

  • Two short written responses.
  • A brief counterfactual question concerning what they would do if they were not offered a place in the Residency.

Applicants should use these responses to demonstrate their reasoning, motivation and ability to think clearly about their proposed work and future trajectory.

MATS Residency Tracks

The Winter 2027 Residency includes several tracks, each intended for different applicant profiles and career stages.

Bridge Track

The Bridge track is particularly relevant to applicants who may be entering AI safety from another field or who need additional time and support to develop their research portfolio.

Applicants for Bridge must provide a research plan explaining:

  • What they intend to work on.
  • Why the research matters.
  • How it could contribute to AI safety.
  • Their theory of change.

Why Bridge?

Applicants should explain why the Residency is particularly valuable at their current stage.

This could involve:

  • Transitioning into AI safety.
  • Developing a research direction.
  • Strengthening an existing body of work.
  • Getting dedicated research time.
  • Addressing hiring constraints.
  • Addressing visa or timing constraints.

Applicants should also explain where they hope to go after the Residency and how participation would help them reach that next stage.

Research Experience and Future Contribution

Applicants should explain how their previous experience prepares them to contribute to AI safety research.

For people transitioning from another field, this is an opportunity to highlight transferable:

  • Research methods.
  • Technical skills.
  • Analytical abilities.
  • Policy expertise.
  • Domain knowledge.
  • Unique perspectives.

Applicants who already have AI safety experience should explain how additional time and support would allow them to deepen their research and prepare for their next opportunity.

Anchor Track

The Anchor track is designed for applicants for whom a longer-term research pathway is the appropriate next step.

Applicants must submit a research plan and provide two referees who have directly supervised or evaluated their work.

Suitable referees may include:

  • Research supervisors.
  • Collaborators.
  • Senior colleagues.
  • Other people with direct knowledge of the applicant’s work.

Why Anchor?

Applicants should explain why a two-year staff researcher pathway is the appropriate next step for them.

They should distinguish this pathway from alternatives such as:

  • A PhD.
  • A postdoctoral position.
  • Another research role.
  • Other professional opportunities.

Evidence of Independent Work

Applicants must demonstrate that they can take ownership of an open-ended problem and make meaningful progress.

Evidence may include:

  • Independent research.
  • A thesis.
  • Industry research.
  • Technical projects.
  • Policy work.
  • Other comparable experience.

Importantly, applicants do not need peer-reviewed publications or previous AI safety experience to demonstrate this capability.

Incubation Track

The Incubation track is intended for applicants seeking to develop a research agenda, research program or organization.

Instead of submitting a conventional research plan, applicants provide a project plan explaining the direction they intend to develop and its theory of change.

Incubation Rationale

Applicants should explain:

  • What is novel about their proposed direction.
  • Why the idea requires dedicated time and support.
  • Why MATS Incubation is an appropriate environment.
  • What they hope to develop during the Residency.

90-Day Plan

Applicants must outline what they intend to test or accomplish during their first 90 days.

A strong plan should also identify what evidence would cause the applicant to:

  • Revise the project.
  • Pause the project.
  • Stop the project altogether.

This demonstrates that the applicant is prepared to learn from evidence rather than simply pursuing a predetermined idea.

Governance and Publication Plan

Where relevant, applicants should discuss:

  • Governance.
  • Publication strategy.
  • Access to research outputs.
  • Information hazards.
  • Dual-use risks.

This is particularly important for projects involving potentially sensitive AI safety research or technologies that could have both beneficial and harmful applications.

Team and Resources

Applicants should identify the expertise and resources required to execute their project.

For projects involving the creation of an organization, applicants should also identify:

  • Roles that still need to be filled.
  • Skills required from future team members.
  • How they would recruit suitable people.

Use of AI Tools in the Application

MATS allows applicants to use AI tools while preparing their applications.

However, applicants are expected to be transparent about their use of AI.

Applicants should:

  1. Briefly disclose whether they used AI tools.
  2. Explain how they used them.
  3. Confirm that they agree to the applicable AI-use policy.
  4. Ensure that the application reflects their own reasoning and judgment.

MATS states that disclosed AI use is not, by itself, a reason for rejection.

The important consideration is whether the application genuinely represents the applicant’s own thinking and work.

This can be particularly useful for applicants whose first language is not English. They may use AI tools to improve the clarity of their writing while retaining responsibility for the substance and reasoning of the application.

Tips for Preparing a Strong MATS Residency Application

Because the Residency emphasizes the quality of work rather than conventional credentials, applicants should focus on demonstrating ability, judgment and potential impact.

1. Develop a Clear Research Idea

Avoid submitting a vague statement about wanting to “work in AI safety.”

Instead, identify a specific problem and explain:

  • What the problem is.
  • Why it matters.
  • What you intend to investigate.
  • What existing approaches fail to address.
  • What your proposed approach adds.
  • What results would change your mind.

2. Focus on the Theory of Change

Your application should make a clear connection between your research and improved AI safety.

Explain how your research could move from:

Research question → findings → practical application → improved safety → reduced catastrophic AI risk.

3. Select Your Strongest Work Sample

Choose the work that best demonstrates your actual capabilities.

A technically sophisticated project, rigorous analysis or strong independent research output may be more useful than simply submitting something because it has a prestigious affiliation.

4. Choose References Carefully

Select people who can provide specific evidence about your abilities.

A referee who has directly observed your research, technical work or analytical skills can potentially provide a much stronger assessment than someone who only knows you superficially.

5. Keep the CV Focused

Because the CV is limited to two pages, applicants should prioritize:

  • Relevant research.
  • Significant projects.
  • Technical or analytical achievements.
  • Publications or substantial outputs.
  • Relevant professional experience.
  • Evidence of independent work.

6. Demonstrate Intellectual Independence

The Residency is interested in people who can tackle difficult, open-ended problems.

Where possible, show examples of situations in which you:

  • Identified an important problem.
  • Developed your own approach.
  • Worked through uncertainty.
  • Produced a substantive result.
  • Changed your view based on evidence.

7. Do Not Overemphasize Credentials

A lack of a PhD or previous AI safety job should not automatically discourage an applicant.

Instead, use the application to demonstrate what you can actually contribute.

8. Contact MATS if You Are Unsure

Applicants who are uncertain about:

  • Their eligibility.
  • The most appropriate track.
  • The appropriate office.
  • The suitability of their research idea.

can contact the MATS Residency team before applying.

The official contact is residency@matsprogram.org.

Why the MATS Residency Winter 2027 Is Worth Considering

The program offers an opportunity for talented individuals to dedicate substantial time to difficult AI safety questions while engaging with an international research community.

Potential advantages include:

  • Developing advanced AI safety research experience.
  • Working on ambitious and potentially high-impact research questions.
  • Connecting with researchers and collaborators.
  • Accessing an established AI safety research environment.
  • Developing a stronger research portfolio.
  • Transitioning from another field into AI safety.
  • Pursuing longer-term research through the Anchor pathway.
  • Developing a new research project or organization through Incubation.
  • Accessing international offices in London, Berkeley and Washington, DC.
  • Receiving visa support where international relocation is required.

The precise experience will depend on the applicant’s selected track, research direction and individual circumstances.

How to Apply for the MATS Residency Winter 2027

Interested applicants should begin by reviewing the official Residency information and application requirements.

The application can be submitted online through the official MATS application system.

MATS Residency Winter 2027 Application

Applicants should make sure they have sufficient time to prepare their research or project plan, identify appropriate referees, select a representative work sample and complete the written responses.

APPLY HERE

Important Dates at a Glance

Stage Date
Winter 2027 application opens 25 August 2026
Application deadline 31 October 2026
Expected application outcome By end of November 2026
Interviews/paid work tests for shortlisted candidates First week of December 2026
Selected Residents informed By end of 2026
Expected Residency start Early 2027
Following application window March 2027

Eligibility and Who Can Apply

Eligible applicant category: International applicants with demonstrated potential to conduct outstanding AI safety research or develop valuable safety-relevant projects.

MATS does not restrict the Residency to people with a particular race, nationality or continent. The program explicitly states that the Residency is open internationally, meaning applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions worldwide may apply, subject to the program’s application and logistical requirements.

Applicants can come from a wide range of professional and academic backgrounds. A PhD, researcher job title, extensive publication record or previous AI safety experience is not required.

Relevant applicants may include:

  • Researchers and academics.
  • Technical professionals.
  • AI and machine-learning specialists.
  • Policy researchers and analysts.
  • Governance and assurance specialists.
  • People transitioning into AI safety.
  • Independent researchers.
  • Professionals with substantial technical or policy work.
  • Entrepreneurs or project founders applying through Incubation.
  • Individuals whose strongest work is confidential or unpublished.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate strong reasoning, research ability, seriousness of purpose and the potential to contribute to reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI.

Visit HERE to learn more about the MATS Residency Winter 2027.

Final Takeaway

The MATS Residency Winter 2027 represents a significant opportunity for people who want to work on some of the most challenging questions surrounding advanced artificial intelligence and its potential risks.

One of the program’s distinguishing features is that it does not rely exclusively on traditional academic credentials. Applicants are assessed primarily on the quality and seriousness of their work and their potential to produce meaningful AI safety research. This creates an opportunity for talented people from academia, industry, policy, technical fields and other backgrounds — including those seeking to transition into AI safety.

The Residency is particularly interested in research involving safe automation of alignment research, AI evaluations and assurance, safety cases, AI strategy, technical AI governance, and agentic and multi-agent AI safety. However, applicants are encouraged to propose other ambitious research directions if they can clearly explain why the work matters and how it could contribute to reducing catastrophic AI risk.

For those considering applying, preparation should begin early. A strong application should contain a focused research or project plan, compelling evidence of previous work, strong references and clear written responses demonstrating independent thinking and sound judgment.

The Winter 2027 application deadline is 31 October 2026, Anywhere on Earth (AoE). Interested applicants should review the official requirements carefully and submit their applications before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Transparency International EU Political Integrity Traineeship 2026 offers an opportunity for an early-career professional to gain practical experience in EU policy, political integrity, anti-corruption research, policy analysis, communications and project support while working with Transparency International EU in Brussels, Belgium.

The six-month traineeship is scheduled to begin on 5 October 2026 and will combine office-based and remote work. The successful trainee will support the organisation’s work on EU political integrity, including monitoring anti-corruption developments, conducting research and analysis, supporting projects and events, tracking activities and impact, and contributing to communication activities.

The position provides a gross monthly traineeship allowance of EUR 1,200, together with additional benefits including holiday entitlement, work-from-home and internet allowances, lunch vouchers, mobile phone subscription, insurance coverage, paid sick leave and full transport allowance.

Applications must be submitted in English by Sunday, 6 September 2026, at 23:59 Brussels time.

About Transparency International EU

Transparency International EU (TI EU) is an international non-profit association operating under Belgian law and based in Brussels, Belgium.

TI EU is part of the wider Transparency International movement, working closely with Transparency International national chapters in more than 100 countries around the world and with the Transparency International Secretariat based in Berlin.

The organisation coordinates Transparency International’s advocacy towards the European Union institutions.

Its mission is focused on:

  • Preventing corruption.
  • Promoting integrity.
  • Promoting transparency.
  • Promoting accountability in EU institutions.
  • Influencing EU policies and legislation.
  • Supporting efforts to fight corruption at national level.
  • Promoting equality and access to justice for citizens.

The EU Political Integrity Traineeship therefore offers an opportunity to work within an organisation whose activities connect European-level policymaking with broader efforts to strengthen integrity, transparency and accountability.

What Is the EU Political Integrity Traineeship 2026?

The EU Political Integrity Traineeship is a six-month early-career traineeship within Transparency International EU.

The successful trainee will work as an EU Policy Trainee and assist the office with its work on EU political integrity.

A major component of the role will involve responding to on-demand policy and research requests from senior team members.

The position provides exposure to a range of activities rather than concentrating on a single area. The trainee may contribute to policy research, anti-corruption monitoring, investigative analysis, events, project implementation, reporting, communications and administrative support.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to graduates and early-career professionals interested in:

  • European Union affairs
  • EU institutions
  • Public policy
  • Political science
  • International relations
  • Law
  • Economics
  • European studies
  • Anti-corruption
  • Transparency and accountability
  • Governance
  • Public-sector integrity
  • Policy research
  • Advocacy
  • Communications

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity Details
Organisation Transparency International EU
Position EU Policy Trainee
Opportunity type Traineeship
Start date 5 October 2026
Duration 6 months
Location Brussels, Belgium
Work arrangement Hybrid: teleworking and office-based work
Working hours 38 hours per week
Contract Convention d’Immersion Professionnelle under Belgian law
Allowance EUR 1,200 gross per month
Application language English
Application deadline 6 September 2026, 23:59 Brussels time
Interview period Week of 14 September 2026
Work experience requirement Early-career applicants; no more than 5+ years of relevant experience
Degree requirement University degree or equivalent experience in a relevant field
Work eligibility Legal right to reside and work in Belgium

What Will the Trainee Do?

The EU Political Integrity Trainee will support Transparency International EU across several areas of its work.

The responsibilities are broad and are intended to provide practical exposure to policy, research, project implementation and organisational activities.

1. Monitor Anti-Corruption Developments

The trainee will monitor developments and trends relating to anti-corruption.

This may involve keeping track of relevant political, policy and institutional developments and identifying information that could be important to Transparency International EU’s work.

This responsibility is particularly relevant for candidates interested in governance, public policy, corruption prevention and European affairs.

2. Conduct Policy Research and Investigative Analysis

The trainee will conduct desk research and investigative analysis of information relevant to anti-corruption work.

This includes examining:

  • Data
  • Trends
  • Stakeholders
  • Policy developments
  • Other anti-corruption-related information

Candidates with previous experience in policy research and analysis will therefore have an advantage, although the source identifies this experience as a plus rather than an absolute requirement.

3. Support Presentations, Meetings and Events

The trainee will help organise:

  • Presentations on Transparency International’s work
  • Internal meetings
  • External events

This responsibility provides practical experience in event coordination and stakeholder engagement while allowing the trainee to understand how a European policy organisation communicates its work.

4. Assist With Project Implementation

The trainee will contribute to the implementation of projects.

This can include providing support for:

  • Project management
  • Project reporting
  • General project activities

The role therefore provides exposure to the operational side of policy and advocacy work in addition to research.

5. Track Activities, Impact and Reporting

The trainee will assist with tracking activities and impact and supporting reporting to external actors.

This responsibility may involve helping the organisation document progress and communicate results to external stakeholders.

It is particularly relevant to applicants who are interested in monitoring, evaluation, reporting and project management.

6. Support Communications

The role includes communication-related responsibilities such as:

  • Proofreading
  • Social media outreach
  • Other communication activities

Applicants with strong written communication skills and an interest in public communication can therefore bring relevant experience to the position.

7. Provide General Office Support

The trainee will also provide overall support to the office, including various administrative tasks.

This means the position requires flexibility and willingness to contribute beyond narrowly defined policy responsibilities.

8. Perform Ad Hoc Duties

The successful candidate may be asked to perform other duties as required.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable working in a small team where responsibilities can vary according to organisational needs.

Educational Qualifications

Applicants should have a university degree or equivalent experience in a relevant discipline.

The source specifically identifies the following fields:

  • European Studies
  • Economics
  • Law
  • Political Sciences
  • International Relations
  • Communications
  • Other social science-related fields

The requirement is therefore relatively broad and allows applicants from several academic backgrounds connected to EU affairs, governance, policy, law, economics, communications and social sciences.

Professional Experience Requirement

The traineeship is intended for people at the start of their careers.

Under the legal traineeship scheme used for the position, candidates should have no more than 5+ years of working experience in this field.

This is an important eligibility consideration for experienced professionals. The position is structured as an early-career traineeship rather than a senior policy or professional role.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider whether their level of professional experience fits within the legal and organisational requirements of the traineeship.

The source also clearly states that the traineeship cannot provide credit required for a degree or diploma.

English Language Requirement

Excellent written and spoken English is required.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in English in professional, research and organisational contexts.

Because the application itself must also be submitted in English, candidates should ensure that their CV and cover letter are professionally written and clearly demonstrate their suitability for the role.

Knowledge of EU Institutions and Policymaking

Applicants must demonstrate knowledge of:

  • European Union institutions
  • EU-level policymaking

This is one of the central requirements of the traineeship.

Candidates should therefore be familiar with how EU institutions function and how policies are developed and implemented at the European level.

Knowledge of EU political processes can be especially useful because the role involves monitoring developments and supporting Transparency International EU’s advocacy and policy work.

Policy Research and Analysis Experience

Previous experience in policy research and analysis is considered an advantage.

Candidates who have:

  • Conducted policy research
  • Analysed political or policy developments
  • Worked with relevant data
  • Produced research outputs
  • Conducted stakeholder analysis
  • Written policy-related reports

may therefore be able to demonstrate a particularly strong fit for the position.

However, the source specifically describes policy research and analysis experience as a plus, rather than listing it as an absolute mandatory requirement.

Organisational and Microsoft 365 Skills

The successful candidate should have excellent organisational skills.

The position also requires proficiency in the use of the Microsoft 365 suite of applications.

Strong organisational ability will be important because the trainee will potentially be working simultaneously on research, meetings, projects, reporting, communications and administrative tasks.

Interest in Anti-Corruption and Transparency

Applicants should have a considerable interest in the work of Transparency International and the field of anti-corruption.

This is an important part of the profile being sought.

Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate genuine interest in issues such as:

  • Corruption prevention
  • Political integrity
  • Transparency
  • Accountability
  • Good governance
  • EU policymaking
  • Institutional integrity

Teamwork and Multicultural Working Environment

The successful candidate should be:

  • A team player
  • Practical in their approach to problem-solving
  • Comfortable working in a small team
  • Able to operate in a multicultural working environment

Because Transparency International EU operates within an international movement and works on European-level issues, the ability to work effectively with people from different backgrounds is important.

Commitment to Transparency International’s Values

Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to the values and goals of Transparency International.

This is particularly relevant because the position involves work directly connected to the organisation’s mission of promoting transparency, integrity and accountability and combating corruption.

Traineeship Salary and Benefits

One of the notable features of this opportunity is that it is a paid traineeship.

The trainee will receive a EUR 1,200 gross monthly traineeship allowance.

In addition, the position includes several benefits.

Benefits include:

  • EUR 1,200 gross monthly traineeship allowance
  • 10 extra-legal days of holiday
  • Work-from-home allowance of EUR 148.73
  • Internet allowance of EUR 20 per month
  • Lunch vouchers worth EUR 8 per working day
  • Mobile phone subscription
  • Hospitalisation insurance
  • Private accident insurance
  • Paid sick leave
  • 100% transport allowance

These benefits make the position particularly attractive for early-career professionals seeking practical experience in Brussels.

Location and Working Arrangement

The traineeship is based in:

Brussels, Belgium

The position offers a combination of:

  • Teleworking
  • Office-based work

This hybrid arrangement provides flexibility while maintaining opportunities for in-person collaboration with the Transparency International EU team.

The position requires a 38-hour working week.

Contract Type

The traineeship will operate under a Convention d’Immersion Professionnelle under Belgian law.

Applicants should understand that this is a specific Belgian legal traineeship arrangement.

The traineeship is intended for candidates at the beginning of their careers and is not designed to provide academic credit toward a degree or diploma.

Starting Date and Duration

The successful candidate is expected to begin the traineeship on:

5 October 2026

The traineeship will last for:

6 months

This provides an opportunity to gain sustained professional experience rather than participating in a short-term internship or brief work placement.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is:

Sunday, 6 September 2026 at 23:59 Brussels time

Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline and should not wait until the final hours, particularly because the application requires both a CV and cover letter.

Interview Timeline

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to participate in an interview during the:

Week of 14 September 2026

Applicants who are shortlisted should therefore remain available during this period.

Due to the large number of applications expected, Transparency International EU states that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Right to Live and Work in Belgium

A critical eligibility requirement is that applicants must have the legal right to reside and work in Belgium.

This means that meeting the educational and professional requirements alone is not sufficient if an applicant does not have the necessary legal status to reside and work in Belgium.

Prospective applicants should verify their own eligibility before applying.

Diversity and Inclusion

Transparency International EU states that it is committed to diversity in its staffing.

The organisation encourages applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, including diversity relating to:

  • Gender
  • Ethnic origin
  • Disability

The source does not identify a racial or ethnic nationality restriction for the traineeship. Instead, it expressly states its commitment to diversity and encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity may be particularly suitable for early-career professionals who want to build a career in EU policy, anti-corruption, governance, transparency, international relations or public affairs.

Strong potential candidates may include graduates and early-career professionals with backgrounds in:

  • European Studies
  • Economics
  • Law
  • Political Science
  • International Relations
  • Communications
  • Social Sciences

Candidates with an interest or experience in policy research, EU policymaking, anti-corruption, advocacy, communications or project support may find the role especially relevant.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted in English.

Applicants are required to complete the application form and submit:

  • A CV
  • A cover letter

The application should clearly demonstrate how the candidate’s education, skills, experience and interests correspond with the requirements of the EU Political Integrity Traineeship.

Prospective applicants should pay particular attention to demonstrating:

  1. Knowledge of EU institutions.
  2. Understanding of EU-level policymaking.
  3. Interest in anti-corruption and political integrity.
  4. Strong English communication skills.
  5. Research and analytical abilities.
  6. Organisational skills.
  7. Ability to work effectively in a multicultural team.
  8. Commitment to Transparency International’s values.

Application form: Apply through the official Transparency International EU application form

Official opportunity page: Transparency International EU – EU Political Integrity Traineeship

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Although the organisation does not provide a scoring rubric in the supplied information, applicants can strengthen their application by making a clear connection between their background and the responsibilities of the position.

1. Tailor Your CV

Your CV should make relevant experience easy to identify.

Where applicable, highlight:

  • EU policy experience
  • Research experience
  • Policy analysis
  • Anti-corruption work
  • Governance projects
  • International relations
  • Advocacy
  • Communications
  • Project management
  • Event organisation
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Data or trend analysis

2. Write a Targeted Cover Letter

The cover letter should not simply repeat the CV.

Instead, explain why you are interested in:

  • Transparency International EU
  • EU political integrity
  • Anti-corruption
  • EU policymaking
  • The specific traineeship

You should also connect your skills to the responsibilities of the role.

3. Demonstrate Your Knowledge of EU Institutions

Since knowledge of EU institutions and EU-level policymaking is required, your application should make this knowledge clear.

Avoid simply stating that you are interested in the European Union. Where possible, demonstrate your understanding through your academic work, professional experience, research, internships, projects or other relevant activities.

4. Highlight Research and Analytical Skills

The position includes desk research and investigative analysis.

Applicants should therefore highlight examples showing their ability to:

  • Find relevant information
  • Analyse evidence
  • Identify trends
  • Research stakeholders
  • Produce written outputs
  • Translate research into useful findings

5. Demonstrate Strong Written English

Because excellent written English is a requirement and applications must be submitted in English, applicants should carefully proofread their CV and cover letter.

Errors in grammar, spelling or structure can make it more difficult for recruiters to assess the candidate’s communication ability.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, candidates should pay particular attention to the following conditions:

  • The position begins on 5 October 2026.
  • The traineeship lasts six months.
  • The role is based in Brussels, Belgium.
  • Hybrid work combining teleworking and office work is offered.
  • The position is 38 hours per week.
  • The monthly allowance is EUR 1,200 gross.
  • Applicants should be at the beginning of their careers.
  • Candidates should have no more than 5+ years of working experience in this field under the relevant traineeship scheme.
  • A university degree or equivalent experience in a relevant discipline is required.
  • Excellent written and spoken English is required.
  • Knowledge of EU institutions and EU policymaking is required.
  • Policy research and analysis experience is an advantage.
  • Applicants must have the legal right to reside and work in Belgium.
  • Applications must be submitted in English.
  • A CV and cover letter are required.
  • The application deadline is 6 September 2026 at 23:59 Brussels time.
  • Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed during the week of 14 September 2026.
  • The traineeship cannot provide academic credit required for a degree or diploma.

Why This EU Policy Traineeship Is Worth Considering

For someone beginning a career in European policy or international governance, this traineeship offers exposure to multiple dimensions of policy work within an international non-profit organisation.

Rather than focusing exclusively on research, the trainee will potentially gain experience across:

  • Policy monitoring
  • Anti-corruption analysis
  • Investigative research
  • Project management
  • Project reporting
  • Events
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Communications
  • Social media
  • Administration
  • Impact tracking

The combination of these responsibilities can help an early-career professional understand how research, advocacy, communications and project implementation interact within a policy-focused organisation.

The Brussels location is another significant feature because the city is home to major EU institutions and a large community of organisations working on European policy.

Pro Tip for Applicants

Do not submit a generic CV and cover letter.

Tailor both documents specifically to the EU Political Integrity Traineeship. Demonstrate your understanding of EU institutions and EU policymaking, connect your research and analytical skills to the anti-corruption focus of the position, and show genuine interest in Transparency International’s mission.

Most importantly, make sure you meet the requirement to legally reside and work in Belgium before investing time in the application.

Click HERE to learn more about the UN Political Integrity Traineeship 2026 in Brussels.

Conclusion

The Transparency International EU Political Integrity Traineeship 2026 is a valuable early-career opportunity for professionals interested in EU policy, anti-corruption, transparency, governance, political integrity and international affairs.

Based in Brussels, the six-month traineeship provides practical experience across policy research, anti-corruption monitoring, investigative analysis, project implementation, reporting, communications, events and administrative support.

The successful candidate will receive a EUR 1,200 gross monthly allowance alongside a substantial package of additional benefits, including holiday entitlement, work-from-home and internet allowances, lunch vouchers, insurance, paid sick leave and full transport allowance.

The opportunity is particularly suited to candidates with university-level education or equivalent experience in European Studies, Economics, Law, Political Science, International Relations, Communications or related social sciences, together with strong English skills, knowledge of EU institutions and policymaking, strong organisational abilities and a genuine interest in anti-corruption.

Applications must be submitted in English with a CV and cover letter by Sunday, 6 September 2026 at 23:59 Brussels time. Applicants must also have the legal right to reside and work in Belgium.

For early-career professionals seeking practical experience at the intersection of European policymaking, political integrity and anti-corruption, this traineeship provides an opportunity to develop professional skills while contributing to the work of a major international anti-corruption movement.

item.content:encoded:
The MOVE Fund 2026 is inviting eligible coalitions and collectives working at the intersection of sport, play, youth development, equity, and community systems to participate in its 2026 funding opportunity. The fund is designed to support collaborative groups seeking to strengthen sport-based youth development, advocate for increased investment in sport and play, and help create local sports systems that are more equitable, positive, and inclusive.

Eligible coalitions and collaboratives can apply for two-year operating grants ranging from $40,000 to $150,000. The opportunity is particularly relevant for organizations and collaborative groups that are working to use sport and play as tools for youth development and broader community change.

Applications for the MOVE Fund 2026 opened on August 24, 2026, and eligible applicants must submit their applications by September 16, 2026.

In addition to the funding opportunity, the MOVE Fund is hosting a MOVE Fund 2026 Webinar on September 2, 2026, where prospective applicants can learn more about the fund and its priorities.

MOVE Fund 2026 Opportunity Details

  • Opportunity: MOVE Fund 2026
  • Category: Grant
  • Grant Type: Two-year operating grant
  • Grant Amount: $40,000 to $150,000
  • Application Opening Date: August 24, 2026
  • Application Deadline: September 16, 2026
  • Webinar Date: September 2, 2026
  • Webinar Time: 8:30 PM Nairobi time
  • Application Structure: One application per coalition or collective
  • Lead Applicant Requirement: The lead organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status

What Is the MOVE Fund?

The MOVE Fund is focused on supporting collaborative efforts that recognize the role that sport and play can play in youth development and community transformation.

Rather than focusing exclusively on individual sports organizations, the fund is intended to support coalitions and collectives working together around broader systems-level goals. These collaborations may bring together organizations, community groups, youth development organizations, advocates, and other stakeholders seeking to improve how sport and play are supported and delivered within their regions.

The fund’s priorities center on three major areas:

  1. Advocating for public and private investment in sport and play
  2. Building the capacity of sport-based youth development organizations
  3. Creating equitable, positive, and inclusive local sports systems

This makes the opportunity potentially valuable for collaborative initiatives that want to move beyond individual programs and contribute to longer-term changes within their local or regional sports ecosystems.

What Will the MOVE Fund Support?

The MOVE Fund will support coalitions and collectives whose work aligns with its stated priorities. Applicants should demonstrate how their collaborative efforts contribute to strengthening sport and play as important tools for youth development and community development.

1. Advocacy for Investment in Sport and Play

One of the key priorities of the MOVE Fund is supporting coalitions that advocate for increased public and private investment in sport and play.

This may be particularly relevant to collaborative groups working to influence:

  • Government investment in sports infrastructure and programming
  • Private-sector investment in sport and youth initiatives
  • Funding for community-based sports programs
  • Policies that improve access to sport and play
  • Investment in youth-focused sports development
  • Greater recognition of sport and play as tools for positive youth development
  • Community-level or regional strategies for strengthening sports ecosystems

Coalitions involved in advocacy should be able to demonstrate how their collective efforts can contribute to stronger investment and support for sport and play.

2. Capacity Building for Sport-Based Youth Development Organizations

The MOVE Fund also seeks to support work that builds the capacity of sport-based youth development organizations.

Capacity building can involve strengthening the ability of organizations to design, implement, manage, evaluate, and sustain programs that use sport and play to support young people.

Collaboratives working in this area may focus on strengthening organizational systems, improving leadership, developing partnerships, enhancing program quality, or building the long-term sustainability of organizations serving young people through sport.

The emphasis on capacity building means that the opportunity is not necessarily limited to organizations delivering sports activities. It can also be relevant to collaborative efforts aimed at strengthening the organizations and systems behind youth sports development.

3. Building Equitable, Positive and Inclusive Local Sports Systems

A third major priority is supporting coalitions that work to create local sports systems that are equitable, positive, and inclusive.

This recognizes that access to sport and play can be influenced by factors such as resources, community infrastructure, organizational capacity, inclusion, and opportunities available to young people.

Coalitions applying to the MOVE Fund should therefore consider how their work contributes to creating sports environments where young people and communities can participate meaningfully and benefit from positive sporting experiences.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful applicants can receive two-year operating grants ranging from $40,000 to $150,000.

The operating-grant structure is important because it indicates that the funding is intended to help support the broader work of eligible coalitions and collectives rather than being limited to a narrowly defined one-time activity.

Depending on the approved grant amount and the needs of the collaborative, funding could provide important support for activities related to advocacy, capacity development, coalition coordination, systems strengthening, and other work aligned with the MOVE Fund’s priorities.

Applicants should carefully review the fund’s official guidance and application requirements before determining the appropriate funding request.

Who Can Apply for the MOVE Fund 2026?

The opportunity is specifically designed for coalitions and collectives/collaboratives whose work aligns with the MOVE Fund’s priorities.

Importantly, the fund states that coalitions or collaboratives at various stages of development are encouraged to apply, provided that their work aligns with the fund’s priorities.

This means that an applicant does not necessarily have to be an established, highly developed coalition to be considered. Emerging and developing collaborative efforts may also be encouraged to apply if they can demonstrate alignment with the fund’s objectives.

Lead Organization Requirement

Although the opportunity is designed around coalitions and collectives, the application must be submitted through one lead organization.

The lead organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status designation.

This is a key eligibility requirement that prospective applicants should consider before beginning the application process.

Coalitions that do not themselves have the required nonprofit status may therefore need to identify an eligible lead organization that can formally submit the application on behalf of the collaborative.

One Application Per Collaborative

The MOVE Fund has established an important application restriction:

Only one application per collaborative or collective can be submitted.

This means that members of the same coalition should coordinate internally before submitting an application.

A coalition should avoid having multiple participating organizations submit separate applications for the same collaborative effort. Instead, the coalition should agree on its lead organization and coordinate the submission as a single collective application.

This makes internal planning and communication particularly important.

Coalitions at Different Stages Are Encouraged to Apply

Another notable feature of the MOVE Fund 2026 opportunity is that coalitions and collaboratives at various stages of development are encouraged to apply, as long as they align with the fund’s priorities.

This can be particularly relevant to emerging partnerships that have begun working together but may not yet have the institutional maturity of long-established networks.

Prospective applicants should therefore focus on demonstrating:

  • A clear collaborative purpose
  • Alignment with the MOVE Fund’s priorities
  • The problem or opportunity the coalition is addressing
  • The role of each participating organization or stakeholder
  • How the collaboration contributes to sport and youth development
  • The potential for positive, equitable, and inclusive change
  • Why the coalition is well positioned to advance its proposed work

MOVE Fund 2026 Webinar

The MOVE Fund is also organizing a webinar for prospective applicants.

Webinar Date and Time

Date: September 2, 2026
Time: 8:30 PM Nairobi time

The webinar can provide an opportunity for interested organizations and coalitions to learn more about the funding opportunity before the application deadline.

Prospective applicants should consider attending if they have questions about the fund, eligibility, application process, priorities, or expectations.

Information Required for Webinar Registration

The registration form asks participants to provide several details, including:

  • First Name
  • Last Name
  • Email Address
  • City
  • Organization
  • Job Title
  • Coalition Name
  • Questions and Comments

Applicants and interested participants should ensure that the information provided during registration is accurate.

The registration information is shared with the account owner and host and may be used and shared according to the applicable terms and privacy policy.

Important MOVE Fund 2026 Dates

Prospective applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

August 24, 2026 — Applications Open

The MOVE Fund 2026 application period officially opened on August 24, 2026.

Applicants can use the period between the opening and closing dates to understand the requirements, coordinate with coalition members, identify the appropriate lead organization, and prepare their submission.

September 2, 2026 — MOVE Fund Webinar

The MOVE Fund 2026 webinar is scheduled for September 2, 2026, at 8:30 PM Nairobi time.

This is an important date for prospective applicants who want to learn more about the opportunity.

September 16, 2026 — Application Deadline

The application period closes on September 16, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to prepare their submission. Coalition members may need time to agree on priorities, gather organizational information, develop the proposal, and ensure that the lead organization meets the nonprofit-status requirement.

How to Prepare a Strong MOVE Fund Application

Although the fund welcomes coalitions and collaboratives at different stages of development, applicants should clearly demonstrate why their work aligns with the MOVE Fund.

1. Clearly Define the Coalition

Begin by explaining who makes up the coalition or collaborative.

Describe:

  • The organizations involved
  • Their respective roles
  • The communities they serve
  • How the organizations complement one another
  • Why collaboration is necessary to achieve the intended results

A strong application should make it easy for reviewers to understand the collective’s structure and purpose.

2. Demonstrate Alignment With MOVE Fund Priorities

Applicants should clearly connect their proposed work to one or more of the fund’s three stated priorities.

Explain whether the coalition is primarily focused on:

  • Advocating for investment in sport and play
  • Building organizational capacity among sport-based youth development organizations
  • Creating equitable, positive, and inclusive local sports systems

If the work addresses more than one priority, applicants should explain how the different components are connected.

3. Explain the Problem Being Addressed

Clearly describe the challenge facing the communities, organizations, or sports system the coalition is seeking to address.

Avoid simply describing the problem in general terms. Explain why it matters and how it affects young people, sports organizations, communities, or the broader local sports ecosystem.

4. Explain Why a Collaborative Approach Is Necessary

Because this is a coalition-focused opportunity, applicants should demonstrate the value of working collectively.

Explain what can be achieved through collaboration that individual organizations would struggle to achieve independently.

This could include:

  • Combining expertise
  • Coordinating advocacy
  • Sharing resources
  • Strengthening organizational capacity
  • Connecting different stakeholders
  • Influencing systems
  • Increasing community participation
  • Creating more sustainable solutions

5. Develop a Clear Two-Year Vision

Since the grants are structured as two-year operating grants, applicants should think beyond short-term activities.

A strong proposal should demonstrate what the coalition hopes to accomplish during the two-year funding period and how its work can contribute to longer-term change.

Consider outlining:

  1. The current situation
  2. The desired change
  3. The activities that will contribute to that change
  4. The organizations responsible for different components
  5. The expected results
  6. How progress will be assessed
  7. How the work can continue beyond the grant period

6. Choose the Lead Organization Carefully

Since only one application can be submitted per collaborative, the coalition should carefully select its lead organization.

The lead organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status designation.

The coalition should ensure that the lead organization is prepared to coordinate the application and meet any administrative, financial, and reporting responsibilities associated with the grant.

Why This Opportunity Matters

The MOVE Fund 2026 could provide substantial financial support to collaborative initiatives using sport and play to promote youth development and strengthen local sports systems.

The potential benefits include:

  • Significant funding: Eligible coalitions can seek two-year operating grants of $40,000 to $150,000.
  • Systems-level support: The fund focuses on strengthening broader local sports systems rather than only individual activities.
  • Capacity development: Funding can support efforts to strengthen sport-based youth development organizations.
  • Advocacy opportunities: Coalitions can advance efforts to increase public and private investment in sport and play.
  • Equity and inclusion: The fund specifically highlights the importance of equitable, positive, and inclusive sports systems.
  • Collaborative development: The opportunity is designed for coalitions and collectives working collectively toward shared objectives.
  • Support for developing collaborations: Coalitions at different stages of development are encouraged to apply when their work aligns with the fund’s priorities.

Who Should Consider This Opportunity?

The MOVE Fund 2026 may be particularly relevant to:

  • Sport-based youth development organizations
  • Coalitions of nonprofit organizations
  • Collaborative youth development initiatives
  • Community organizations working through sport and play
  • Organizations advocating for greater investment in sports
  • Networks seeking to strengthen local sports systems
  • Groups working to improve equity and inclusion in sport
  • Organizations building the capacity of youth sports programs
  • Emerging and established collaboratives aligned with the MOVE Fund priorities

However, prospective applicants should carefully review the official MOVE Fund requirements, particularly the requirement that the application be submitted through a lead organization with 501(c)(3) nonprofit status designation.

APPLY HERE 

Frequently Asked Questions About the MOVE Fund 2026

What is the MOVE Fund 2026?

The MOVE Fund 2026 is a grant opportunity supporting coalitions and collectives working to advance investment in sport and play, strengthen sport-based youth development organizations, and create equitable, positive, and inclusive local sports systems.

How much funding can applicants receive?

The grants are two-year operating grants ranging from $40,000 to $150,000.

Is this a one-year grant?

No. The opportunity provides two-year operating grants.

Can more than one application be submitted by the same collaborative?

No. Only one application per collaborative or collective can be submitted.

Does the coalition need a lead organization?

Yes. The coalition or collective must apply through one lead organization.

What status must the lead organization have?

The lead organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status designation.

Are only established coalitions eligible?

The MOVE Fund states that coalitions or collaboratives at various stages of development are encouraged to apply, provided their work aligns with the fund’s priorities.

When did applications open?

Applications opened on August 24, 2026.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is September 16, 2026.

When is the MOVE Fund webinar?

The webinar will take place on September 2, 2026, at 8:30 PM Nairobi time.

Where can applicants find more information?

Visit HERE to learn more about the MOVE Fund 2026.

Final Thoughts

The MOVE Fund 2026 presents an opportunity for coalitions and collectives seeking to use sport and play as mechanisms for youth development, organizational strengthening, advocacy, and community-level systems change.

With two-year operating grants of $40,000 to $150,000, the opportunity could provide meaningful resources for collaborative groups working to increase investment in sport and play, strengthen sport-based youth development organizations, and build sports systems that are more equitable, positive, and inclusive.

One of the most important requirements to remember is that only one application can be submitted per collaborative, and the application must be submitted through a lead organization with 501(c)(3) nonprofit status designation. Prospective applicants should therefore coordinate early with their coalition members and ensure that the lead organization is prepared to submit the application.

The September 2, 2026 webinar at 8:30 PM Nairobi time also provides an important opportunity for prospective applicants to learn more about the fund. Interested coalitions should use the remaining application period to review the requirements, strengthen their collaborative proposal, and submit their application before the September 16, 2026 deadline.
